articles.excerpt: Your ingestion job is green. Your job assistant is still quoting yesterday's requirements from a posting whose id hasn't changed. Only-new monitoring is an identity feed; refreshing existing answers r…
articles.body: Your ingestion job is green. Your job assistant is still quoting yesterday's requirements from a posting whose id hasn't changed. Only-new monitoring is an identity feed; refreshing existing answers requires comparing their content. Lab note 136: can a daily job feed keep role answers current? The catch comes first: the API provides no update or closed-job timestamp. We need repeated observations to notice a rewrite, and those observations can't tell us when the employer made it. What did your daily refresh actually refresh? The job-board Actor's onlyNewSinceLastRun option emits postings unseen by an earlier run with the same query shape. The first run returns everything. That's useful for new-role alerts.

articles.title: Checking Borat quotes with Python's difflib: Wikiquote vs the film transcript
articles.excerpt: Most movie quote pages copy each other. One site types a line from memory, another copies it, and soon "Very nice!" is followed by words nobody in the film ever said. For our Borat quotes page we used…
articles.body: Most movie quote pages copy each other. One site types a line from memory, another copies it, and soon "Very nice!" is followed by words nobody in the film ever said. For our Borat quotes page we used a simple rule: a film line goes on the page only if two separate texts agree on it. The first is Wikiquote. The second is a transcript of the film. A short Python script decides whether they agree. Of the 97 Borat lines the script checked, 74 passed. This post covers how it decides, why the other 23 failed, and a mistake the check missed that I found while writing this. The two witnesses Witness 1: Wikiquote. We fetch each film's page as wikitext ( action=raw ) and parse it into JSON: one record per line, with the speaker and the film.

articles.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. Rather, it will go on display as a museum piece, according to company founder and CEO Elon Musk.
articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: The Comment That Ruined My Thursday
articles.excerpt: 09:12. I open the pull request and there it is, three words under a line of my code, in red. "This is wrong." No line number beyond the one it sits on. No "because". No "try this instead". Just the th…
articles.body: 09:12. I open the pull request and there it is, three words under a line of my code, in red. "This is wrong." No line number beyond the one it sits on. No "because". No "try this instead". Just the three words, and a name beside them I recognise from the team list, and a little grey timestamp that says it arrived at 08:47, twenty-five minutes before I got to my desk. I read it again. Then I read it a third time, slower, as if the extra words might be hiding between the three that are there. They are not. The line it sits on is mine. It sorts a list of invoices by date, and I wrote it on Tuesday afternoon, in a hurry, because the dashboard needed it and the afternoon was already gone. I remember writing it.

articles.body: When you build a personal finance app, you start with the features you think will be hardest: Room database encryption with SQLCipher. On-device machine learning classifiers. Multi-threaded SMS regex pipelines. You assume that tracking loans to friends will be the easiest feature in the entire project. After all, it's just basic arithmetic: $\text{lent} - \text{repaid} = \text{balance}$. I could not have been more wrong. Over the development journey of FinLedger—from early v1.0 prototypes to our comprehensive v2.1 architectural audit ( docs/audit/FINLEDGER_FEATURE_AUDIT_MASTER.md )—the Lending and Borrowing Subsystem underwent more complete rewrites and structural refactorings than almost any other module in the codebase.

articles.excerpt: The typical small business owner loses 14 hours a week to tasks that software could do faster, better, and without a single sick day. It never shows up as waste on the income statement. It vanishes in…
articles.body: The typical small business owner loses 14 hours a week to tasks that software could do faster, better, and without a single sick day. It never shows up as waste on the income statement. It vanishes into payroll, written off as "just doing the job." Consider a 5-person service business paying an average of $25 an hour. It spends $10,000 to $15,000 a month on administrative overhead alone, and most of that can be automated. The figure doesn't come from big, memorable tasks. It comes from two-minute chores that repeat fifty times a week: manually logging a lead into a CRM, sending the same welcome email with one name swapped, building a weekly report from three different spreadsheets, or chasing an invoice that has sat unpaid for eleven days. None of these is a complex problem.

articles.title: How Rockstar Made Every NPC Feel Alive in GTA 6
articles.excerpt: Rockstar made NPCs feel alive in GTA 6 by "establishing deep backstories for almost everything" throughout Leonida.
articles.body: Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there. GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments.

articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

The website RansomwareHelp urged victims “Do not pay the ransom!,” claiming its advanced cryptographic tools could restore 100 percent of data, servers, and systems to their original format, and that there was no need to give in to extortion demands.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.
